tier_reason: The README's only baseline statement is the prose line that the misa77 format decodes '1.5-2x faster than LZ4', with no numbers or setup; its Performance tables (first 1 MiB of 12 Silesia files, x86_64 AVX2, best of 10 rounds) compare m77rip only against the vendored misa77 v0.6.0 C++ reference, so there are no numbers against lz4 or any other listed baseline. The m77rip table numbers in the record match the page exactly.

corrections.caveats: No numeric comparison against lz4, zstd or any listed baseline in this repo; the only lz4 statement is the unsupported '1.5-2x faster than LZ4' prose about the misa77 format. The README tables compare m77rip with the vendored misa77 v0.6.0 C++ reference (built via build.rs with -msse2/-mavx2 dispatch TUs; Rust flags and CPU model not stated): default-build decode is 0.87x-0.91x of misa77, the paranoid (no-unsafe) build decodes at 0.22x-0.44x, and encode ranges 0.90x-1.70x (faster only at levels 2-4). Compressed ratio is identical to misa77 (same format). The bench/ directory holds only a chart generator (bench/src/bin/m77rip_charts.rs, plotters-based) that reads cached rows produced by an m77rip_bench binary with --features c-reference; that binary was not located in bench/. 7 stars, 0 forks. Same format as misa77, so it is a Rust reimplementation (port) of an already-listed codec, not a distinct codec.

notes: m77rip is a memory-safe Rust reimplementation of the misa77 format (same bitstream, same levels -1 to 4, identical ratios, vendors misa77 C++ as reference), not a distinct codec; recommend decision 'duplicate' folding into https://github.com/welcome-to-the-sunny-side/misa77 per the ports/bindings rule, or keep as tier D with the shortcoming that it is slower than misa77 on decode.
